statement: Four data sets are shown in the choices below. Which data set has the greatest standard deviation?

choices.misconception: I picked the set with the largest range, 32, but four of its six values sit right at the mean, so its typical distance from the mean is small.
I thought evenly spaced values with no repeats are the most spread out, but most of them are close to the mean of 20.
I picked the set with the biggest numbers, but standard deviation measures spread around the mean, not how large the values are.

hints: Standard deviation measures how far values typically are from the mean.
Find each set's mean, then compare how far the values are from that mean. A large range alone does not guarantee a large spread.
In the set $8, 8, 8, 32, 32, 32$, every value is $12$ from the mean of $20$. In the set with range $32$, only two values are away from $20$ at all.

solutions.reliable: Find each mean and the distances from it. The set $4, 20, 20, 20, 20, 36$ has mean $20$ and distances $16, 0, 0, 0, 0, 16$. The set $8, 8, 8, 32, 32, 32$ has mean $20$, and every distance is $12$. The set $10, 14, \ldots, 30$ has mean $20$ and distances $10, 6, 2, 2, 6, 10$. The set $80, 82, \ldots, 90$ has mean $85$ and distances $5, 3, 1, 1, 3, 5$. The sums of squared distances are $512$, $864$, $280$ and $70$. Every set has $6$ values, so the largest sum gives the largest standard deviation: $8, 8, 8, 32, 32, 32$, whose standard deviation is exactly $12$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
